answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 6 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The ember multiplier is published, charged in pigment, and ocean lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 3514 identities would post 1976 proofs and burn roughly 3 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
